newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - S.Elec yr profits in line, eyes value.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - S.Elec yr profits in line, eyes value.

text.p: Britain's last remaining independent regional electricity company (Rec) Southern Electric Plc on Wednesday turned in lower year-end profits but within analysts' expectations, and said it was committed to maximising shareholder value through its strong balance street.
Finance Director Ian Marchant told Reuters the company had no immediate plans on returning value but was "awaiting to see how things evolve over the next few weeks".
Southern said pretax profits for the year ending March 31 were 255.5 million pounds ($417 million) compared with 283 million a year ago, as it felt the impact of regulatory price reviews.
Southern's shares gained five pence to 403.5 pence by 1008 GMT, just off a day's high of 405 pence.
Southern spent around 156 million pounds on a shareholder buyback deal earlier this year after being outbid by Scottish Power in a takeover tussle for Southern Water last year.
Its own plans to merge with generator National Power were frustrated when the previous Conservative government blocked the deal as anti-competitive over a year ago.

Southern, along with other privatised utilities, could be subject to a one-off tax proposed by the new Labour government on excess profits aimed at funding a three billion pound scheme to cut unemployment.
Details of the scheme, including amounts and companies affected, are expected in the July 2 budget.
Marchant, who described the so-called "windfall" tax as "political," said Southern had made representations to the government over the tax but declined to elaborate.

He ruled out pressure on the company to use the strength of its balance sheet to make an acquisition, adding that Southern was "confident" its existing businesses would allow dividend growth of five to eight percent in real terms over the next three years.
Southern said in a statement that it was working to a clear strategy of growth for its four key businesses -- distribution, supply, generation and contracting.
It said that it should achieve long-term profitable earnings growth through profit contribution from non-regulated earnings and plans for future investment in generation.
Southern said plans for two 45-megaWatt (mW) open-cycle gas-fired power stations were well advanced with a further five sites identified for similar plants.
It will be investing around 100 million pounds in these projects over the next few years and Marchant said they should provide "quite significant earnings growth from 2000 and beyond."
Southern's maximum demand last year was 5,700 mW, he said.
He added that the company was also looking outside its own area for generation possibilities.
In distribution, Marchant said there was "more to go for in reducing costs," but declined to set targets.
Southern also expects liberalisation of the domestic market, scheduled to start in April 1998, to be an area of opportunity, claiming to be "well placed for growth as a leading national supplier."

Marchant said the company was "still talking quite seriously to two or three people" about link-ups with a national brand to tackle liberalisation, "and if there is a commercial deal to be done, we'll do it."

Southern would be ready to enter testing of the market in January, he said, and was "entirely confident" of being ready on time for the opening up of the market from April, he added. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
